conclusion: Confirmed execution-integrity information gap, not a confirmed reward-misclassification bug: exit1 bypasses upstream JUnit validation and current _verify accepts partially observed/error/skip reports. Whether reward0 is wrong depends on failure causation and the explicitly selected terminal-reward contract. Agent-induced source/import/setup/collection failures may be legitimate official failures; deleting them would introduce action-dependent censoring. No actual contamination was found in four examined R3 exit1 rewards, all backed by complete declared required-node coverage and assertion failures.
minimal_recommendation: Do not change reward/admission from exit1 missing/error/skip alone. Keep official resolved and existing historical rewards immutable; the prior blanket unknown proposal is withdrawn.

If adding information, keep one execution-observation summary separate from reward: declared required-node presence, failure/error/skip counts, and collector/process status. These facts do not by themselves prove environment failure or a known terminal return.

Use the fixed, byte-bound reviewed-repair control as evidence that the runtime can execute the intended oracle. A passing reviewed repair supports interpreting agent-only breakage as a genuine failed patch, but a single pass cannot rule out transient external failures. A failing control at the same runtime with the same infrastructure failure supports unknown; compare exact failure phase/module and immutable task/snapshot/oracle/runtime pins.

Keep normal fully observed assertion failure1 as valid0, including all-required-failed. Do not use upstream _validate_junit_xml as a completeness predicate: it rejects failures and zero-pass reports by design.

If a prospective study explicitly requires all required calls to execute, label that as a new conditional objective/admission rule, quantify action-dependent exclusions, and do not call improvement after filtering a repair gain. Do not add this new filter to current training by inference.

For any required-node observation, use declared parameter identity and source/class identity carefully. The official short-name fallback can conflate parameter cases; a bare parametrized function does not enumerate all parameter expansions. This is a measurement boundary, not authorization to rewrite the oracle.

superseded_initial_interpretation.conclusion: Confirmed reachable classification defect: upstream skips JUnit validation for exit1, and actual current _verify accepts nonempty partially executed/error/skipped required results as reward0. In the four real R3 exit1 outcomes inspected, every declared requirement was present with no error/skip; no actual historical reward contamination was found in this narrow review.
recommendation: Parse the copied JUnit on exit0 and exit1 before assigning verification_complete; do not call _validate_junit_xml as a completeness predicate because it deliberately rejects ordinary assertion failures and reports with zero passes.

Require each declared F2P/P2P requirement to have an actual matching testcase; for a bare function requirement allow its real parameterized cases, but keep explicitly declared parameter IDs and source/class identity exact. Missing/error/skipped required nodes are unknown rather than invented zero.
Preserve exit1 + fully executed required nodes with failure tags as a valid zero, including all-required-failed cases. Preserve official resolved logic and do not replace original oracle acceptance.

Document the limit: a bare parametrized function requirement does not enumerate its full parameter expansion, so membership alone cannot prove every unlisted parameter ran; fail-fast/interrupt completeness may require a trusted collection inventory or clear process/collection/summary evidence.
superseded_initial_interpretation.reason: Root correctly identified that execution completeness and failure attribution are different. A bad production patch can itself cause import/setup/collection errors or policy-dependent skip/missing nodes. Automatically censoring every such official failure would delete bad actions and alter the learning estimand. The synthetic aggregation examples establish what the classifier accepts, not that those zero rewards are wrong.

command_and_causation_boundary.official_command: cd /workspace && PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 python3 -s -m pytest <unchanged explicit target files> --junitxml=<uuid.xml> -p no:anyio -o timeout=0 -o python_classes="Test* *Test" -q
command_and_causation_boundary.evidence: adk_eval_core build_sanitized_env only inherits its _SAFE_ENV_KEYS, which do not include PYTEST_ADDOPTS. swegemma SubprocessManager adds VIRTUAL_ENV/PATH/PYTHONPATH. Existing [pytest] ini configuration may be preserved by setup_workspace_test_config.
command_and_causation_boundary.default_collection_failure: Pinned pytest pytest_runtestloop raises Interrupted when session.testsfailed and continue_on_collection_errors is false: ordinary collection failure normally yields exit2. With continue enabled, _main can return TESTS_FAILED/exit1. Explicit official command does not enable continue; source config/plugins can, but no such option was observed in the 16 examined R3 root config sets.
command_and_causation_boundary.default_fixture_failure: Pinned pytest JUnit writer records call-phase failures as <failure>, setup/teardown failures as <error>; these run failures can return exit1 without --continue-on-collection-errors. Both agent production-code failures and infrastructure failures can produce these outcomes.
command_and_causation_boundary.early_stop: Pinned pytest maxfail raises Failed→TESTS_FAILED/exit1 after partial execution. The official command does not set maxfail and no --maxfail/-x was observed in the examined R3 root config sets. Plugins or other unexamined configuration are not ruled out.
command_and_causation_boundary.synthetic_collection_only_exit_one: This fixture is an explicitly constructed aggregation case, not an observation of default pytest collecting with exit1. It must not be presented as an actually reproduced task or default runtime behavior.
command_and_causation_boundary.protected_oracle: Tests/conftest/pytest.ini/pyproject/tox/setup.cfg are protected from agent patch sections, but production source remains editable and can break test imports, fixture setup or feature-dependent skip behavior.
command_and_causation_boundary.control_location: Current run.py collection verifies host-only submitted.patch as focal-environment-control after an original episode with known reward/candidate, and excludes that original when reviewed control reward!=1. Preparation also binds task/snapshot/isolation. This is useful environment evidence, not a same-patch counterfactual for every branch or an omniscient failure-cause classifier.
command_and_causation_boundary.existing_boundary: Current exit2/4/-1/timeout unknown filtering already can exclude agent-caused failures as well as environment failures. This audit does not authorize broadening or silently fixing that existing reward contract; it should be described as a conditional coverage limit.
